text: The second spirit was a jolly giant. <break time="0.8s" /> In a green robe. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding a glowing torch. <break time="0.8s" /> He took Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> To the small house of his clerk, Bob Cratchit. <break time="0.8s" /> Bob earned only fifteen shillings a week. <break time="0.8s" /> But his family was full of joy. <break time="0.8s" /> They shared a small goose and a pudding. <break time="0.8s" /> And nobody said. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was small. <break time="0.8s" /> Bobs little son, Tiny Tim. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a weak boy. <break time="0.8s" /> Who walked with a crutch. <break time="0.8s" /> God bless us, every one. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Tiny Tim. <break time="0.8s" /> At the end of dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> Spirit, tell me. <break time="0.8s" /> If Tiny Tim will live. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Scrooge with new interest. <break time="0.8s" /> If these shadows stay the same. <break time="0.8s" /> The child will die. <break time="0.8s" /> Answered the spirit. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the spirit repeated. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooges own cold words. <break time="0.8s" /> And Scrooge hung his head in shame. <break time="0.8s" /> Next they visited Freds merry party. <break time="0.8s" /> Where everyone was laughing and playing games. <break time="0.8s" /> Fred felt sorry for his uncle. <break time="0.8s" /> Because Scrooge only hurt himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooge enjoyed the games so much. <break time="0.8s" /> That he begged to stay longer.
